newsitem.title: USA: Japan banks grow weaker with the Nikkei - Barron's.
newsitem.headline: Japan banks grow weaker with the Nikkei - Barron's.

text.p: The fall in Japan's Nikkei stock index is hitting some of the country's top banks hard, and if the slide continues, will hurt more banks, according to analysts quoted in the Monday edition of Barron's.

The article said the drop in stock prices could hinder the banks' efforts to cover bad loan losses and maintain capital reserves at international standards. It also noted that in the past banks have used unrealized capital gains on stocks to improve their balance sheets. With the Nikkei's plummet, those unrealized gains on stocks are narrowing and some banks even have unrealized losses, the article said.

James Fiorillo, of ING Barings Japan, said that with the Nikkei 225 index at the 18,000 level, some banks, including Nippon Credit Bank Ltd, Long-Term Credit Bank of Japan Ltd, Yasuda Trust & Banking Co Ltd and Chuo Trust & Banking Co Ltd , are already in the "danger zone."
The Nikkei closed Friday at 18,090.04, and more nervous trading is foreseen.
If the Nikkei falls to the 17,000 level, Fiorillo said Mitsui Trust & Banking Co Ltd joins the list of worries.
If the Nikkei hits 16,000, Sakura Bank Ltd, Tokai Bank Ltd, Industrial Bank of Japan Ltd, Mitsubishi Bank Ltd, Sumitomo Bank Ltd and Toyo Trust & Banking Co Ltd also enter vulnerable territory.
In the Barron's article, Fiorillo said ING Barings Japan is advising its clients to be underweighted in the Japanese banking sector, except for Mitsubishi-Bank of Tokyo and Asahi Bank.

In the article, Kathy Matsui, chief strategist at Goldman Sachs Japan, said the current weakness in Japan's financial markets could lead to a flight by investors to quality stocks. Those stocks include: Toyota Motor Corp, Honda Motor Co Ltd, Bridgestone Corp, Hoya Corp, Jusco Co Ltd, TDK Corp, Hirose Electric Co Ltd, Canon Inc, Keihin Seiki Manufacturing Co Ltd, Rohm Co Ltd, Futaba Industrial Co Ltd and Santen Pharmaceutical Co Ltd.

The article also quotes Edwin Merner, investment adviser to the $150 million Atlantis Japan Growth fund, as bullish on Sony Corp, NEC Corp, Tokyo Electron Ltd, Innotech Corp, Aderans Co Ltd, Kuroganeya Co Ltd and Sankyo Co Ltd.
